name: Commodore 64
credits: Layout after the Commodore 64 (1982) breadbin keyboard; colours after its brown case, dark brown keys and lighter function keys.
notes: Faithful: all 66 keys of the breadbin in their rows and order, with f1/f3/f5/f7 as the separate column on the right in the lighter grey-brown, upper-case off-white legends on dark brown keys, the shifted characters (! " # $ % & ' ( ) over the digits, [ ] over : ;, < > ? over , . /) and the shifted functions (f2, INST, CLR, RUN) on the key tops, the PETSCII graphics and colour names on the key fronts, and a blank space bar. The front graphics use the nearest Unicode box, block and card characters (Commodore-key graphic left, shifted graphic right); where there is no close one (O, P, L, @, * and others) the front is left bare. Letters type lower case and SHIFT upper case so a parser can read them; the C64's own upper-case/graphics mode is not reproduced. ← types _ and ↑ types ^, the ASCII characters at their PETSCII positions. The cursor keys move down and right, and up and left with SHIFT, as on the machine; INST/DEL erases; CLR/HOME is escape; SHIFT LOCK locks shift. f1, f3, f5 and f7 are up, down, left and right, one tap each where the cursor keys need SHIFT for up and left. Approximated: widths are compressed to fit a phone, the keys are drawn rather than photographed, and the Commodore logo is the text C=. Mapped to none: RUN/STOP and RESTORE (they stop or reset a BASIC program), CTRL and C= (no control or graphics layer).
